review.zebra-medical.faq.1.question.what: What conditions can Zebra Medical Vision detect?
review.zebra-medical.faq.1.answer.zebras: Zebra's algorithm library includes detection for cardiovascular disease (coronary calcium, aortic calcification), liver conditions (hepatic steatosis/fatty liver), bone health (osteoporosis, compression fractures), lung pathologies (emphysema, nodules), and various other conditions. The platform currently offers 12+ validated algorithms with more in development. Each algorithm targets specific anatomical findings or disease markers visible on CT, MRI, or X-ray imaging. The comprehensive screening approach means a single chest CT might be analyzed for cardiovascular, pulmonary, and bone conditions simultaneously.
How accurate is Zebra Medical Vision?
review.zebra-medical.faq.2.answer.zebras: Zebra's algorithms demonstrate high accuracy metrics in clinical validation studies, typically with sensitivity and specificity exceeding 90% for most conditions. Performance varies by specific algorithm and condition - some like coronary calcium detection have near-perfect accuracy, while others for more subtle findings may have moderate sensitivity with high specificity to minimize false alarms. The algorithms are trained on millions of imaging studies representing diverse patient populations. Zebra publishes peer-reviewed validation studies demonstrating real-world performance. Like all AI tools, accuracy depends on image quality and appropriate clinical use.
review.zebra-medical.faq.3.answer.no.zeb: No, Zebra Medical Vision is designed to assist radiologists, not replace them. The platform acts as an automated screening and prioritization tool that flags potential findings for radiologist review. Final diagnosis and clinical reporting remain the radiologist's responsibility. Zebra's value is in detecting incidental findings that might be overlooked, ensuring urgent cases are prioritized, and providing a safety net for quality assurance. Studies show AI-assisted radiology combines the best of algorithmic consistency with human clinical judgment for optimal patient outcomes.
Zebra Medical Vision requires integration with your PACS (Picture Archiving and Communication System) to receive imaging studies and deliver results. The AI processing can be deployed either cloud-based or on-premise depending on your preferences and security requirements. Cloud deployment requires reliable internet connectivity for uploading studies and receiving analyses. On-premise deployment requires local server infrastructure. Zebra provides technical support for integration with major PACS vendors including GE, Philips, Siemens, and others. IT teams typically complete implementation within several weeks to months depending on complexity.
review.zebra-medical.faq.5.question.is.z: Is Zebra Medical Vision FDA approved?
Zebra Medical Vision algorithms have CE marking for use in Europe and regulatory clearances in various countries. Several algorithms have received FDA clearance in the United States for specific indications. The regulatory status varies by algorithm and geographic region. Zebra continues expanding regulatory approvals across its algorithm portfolio. CE marking indicates the platform meets European safety and performance requirements for medical devices. Hospitals should verify specific algorithm approvals in their jurisdiction before clinical deployment.
How is Zebra Medical Vision priced?
Zebra uses customized enterprise pricing based on hospital size, imaging volume, selected algorithms, and deployment model. Pricing models include per-study fees, annual licensing, or unlimited-use subscriptions. The all-in-one platform approach often provides better value than purchasing multiple single-condition AI tools separately. Exact pricing varies significantly by implementation - a large academic medical center will have different pricing than a mid-sized community hospital. Contact Zebra directly for a quote tailored to your organization's specific needs and volume. Many hospitals find ROI through improved quality metrics, reduced liability, and operational efficiency gains.
